title: Exterior acts mostly shared—except sacrifice, temples, altars, and priests reserved to latria
source_text: XII. Sed quantum ad actus exteriores dicunt non esse facile distinguere Duliam a Latria. Quoniam omnes fere actus exteriores quibus uterque cultus exhibetur communes sunt tam Duliae quam Latriae. Excipiunt tamen Sacrificium, & quae ad illud referuntur, templa, altaria, sacerdotes, quae ad solum Latriae cultum pertinere existimant. Nec enim licere cuiquam sacrificium offerre quam Deo, & templa, altaria, Sacerdotes, dicare.
pass_a_gloss: But as regards exterior acts they say it is not easy to distinguish Dulia from Latria. Because nearly all exterior acts by which either cult is exhibited are common to both Dulia and Latria. Yet they except Sacrifice, and the things that are referred to it—temples, altars, priests—which they judge to pertain to the cult of Latria alone. For it is not lawful for anyone to offer sacrifice except to God, and to dedicate temples, altars, Priests.
pass_b_english: Outwardly almost every cult-sign is shared between dulia and latria.
They reserve sacrifice—and temples, altars, priests tied to it—to latria alone.
No one may offer sacrifice or dedicate those things except to God.

choices.why: The exception-cluster Rome ties to latria.
